union.aboutDescription: The Egyptian Tourism Federation is a professional federation established by Law No. 85 of 1968 and amended by Law No. 27 of 2023 to serve the common interests of the tourism sector in the Arab Republic of Egypt.

vision.title: Vision
vision.description: The Egyptian Tourism Federation believes in the importance of the tourism industry and considers it a driver of economic, social, and cultural development.

mission.title: Mission
mission.description: To be a leader in supporting and enhancing the tourism sector through coordination and collaboration among the various tourism chambers.

homePage.unionHeadSpeakDesc: Dear colleagues, My colleagues and I are honored to take on the responsibility of this entity that has stood for many years and has become one of the oldest contributing institutions in Egypt, if not the oldest. Today, I stand before you to present this report, which reflects our efforts and goals since assuming this responsibility, which began nearly one hundred working days ago and will conclude on June 30. The board has set the objectives of this term as follows: First, effective participation in shaping the roadmap for Egyptian tourism to achieve the state's goal of welcoming thirty million tourists annually by 2030, and the required measures to achieve that. In this regard, I extend sincere thanks and appreciation to H.E. the Prime Minister, Dr. Mostafa Madbouly, who personally participated in all meetings and relevant committees, including the Tourism Advisory Committee chaired by him, in which I had the honor to serve alongside a limited number of esteemed tourism investors in Egypt. This committee conducted an in-depth study of the procedures needed to advance the tourism industry and realize the desired goals. The Federation has dedicated all its experts, including council members and administrative staff, to support this committee, which will benefit the sector and Egypt as a whole. I cannot end this message without expressing my deepest gratitude and appreciation to the man who has dedicated his life to ensuring safety and security—without which there would be no tourism industry—His Excellency President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi, President of the Arab Republic of Egypt, who is the primary supporter of the revival and security of Egyptian tourism, after the support of God Almighty. Finally, I thank you all and pray that God grants us success in what is best for Egypt and its people. — Hossam El Shaer. I also extend my gratitude to the esteemed ministers of Interior, Water Resources and Irrigation, Housing, Local Development, Health, Aviation, and the governors, especially those of the tourist provinces. Thirdly, we aim to enforce the laws issued regarding tourism chambers and the Federation, as well as the law on hotel and tourism establishments. I must thank all those who contributed to drafting these laws, starting with the former board members of the Federation under the chairmanship of Mr. Ahmed El-Wassif, the legal advisors, the Tourism and Aviation Committee in Parliament led by Mrs. Nora Ali, legal consultants, and investors from the Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities, under the sponsorship of the concerned ministers. The Federation has ensured that members of the General Assembly are kept informed of all activities and committee work through press releases and periodic newsletters issued by the newly established Media Unit, which aims to keep the tourism sector informed and facilitate coordination between the five tourism chambers—not only to share news, but to support decision-makers with data and well-formed insights on industry-related matters. The Federation has also involved General Assembly members in the specialized committees on investment and relief, based on our firm belief that each of you is a model for the tourism sector in your area of specialization.
homePage.unionDesc: The Federation aims to assist the Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities in formulating the general policy for tourism activities and implementing the national strategy for sustainable tourism, which includes a new roadmap for Egyptian tourism aimed at supporting sustainable tourism development as a driver of economic growth and comprehensive development.

divingroom.title: Tourism Rooms
divingroom.header: Chamber of Diving and Marine Activities
divingroom.description: It includes diving facilities licensed by the Ministry of Tourism. The chamber aims to improve the quality, safety, and standards of diving and marine activity services, in addition to preserving the unique marine life of the Red Sea.

eatroom.title: Tourism Rooms
eatroom.header: Chamber of Tourism Establishments and Restaurants
eatroom.description: It includes tourism establishments licensed by the Ministry of Tourism and works to support and improve the services provided by these establishments and restaurants.

hotelroom.title: Tourism Rooms
hotelroom.description: It includes hotel establishments licensed by the Ministry of Tourism. The chamber works to develop the hotel sector in Egypt by promoting knowledge sharing, overcoming obstacles to its growth, and providing continuous professional training to enhance hotel staff performance.

productroom.title: Tourism Rooms
productroom.header: Chamber of Handicrafts and Tourist Goods
productroom.description: It includes licensed establishments for selling handicrafts and tourist goods. The chamber supports its members and their activities in the trade of tourist products, aiming to develop the product, raise the standards of workers, solve issues, and represent them before the relevant authorities.

travelroom.title: Tourism Rooms
travelroom.header: Chamber of Travel and Tourism Companies
travelroom.description: It includes tourism companies licensed by the Ministry of Tourism. The chamber works to support and care for these companies within the state's tourism plan, and represents them before public authorities, organizations, and local and international bodies.

doubleLearning.title: Learning Management System by the Egyptian Tourism Federation
doubleLearning.subtitle: (Project funded by the German Agency for International Cooperation - GIZ)
doubleLearning.description: Education is one of the key drivers of economic development in Egypt. Technical and vocational education and training (TVET), especially through the dual education system that has been in place since 1994, helps provide a skilled workforce for the labor market. A comprehensive TVET system positively impacts economic growth and institutional productivity. Recognizing the importance of TVET, Article (20) of the 2014 Egyptian Constitution states: (The state is committed to encouraging, developing, and expanding all types of technical education and vocational training in accordance with global quality standards and labor market needs). The Federation therefore sought to have a say in technical education to ensure graduates from technical schools in Egypt meet the required standards for the tourism sector. Consequently, an agreement was signed between the Federation and the Ministry of Education and Technical Education granting the Federation membership in the steering council of the dual education and training system to participate in curriculum design and student training during their studies. This includes hands-on training at various tourism establishments, especially hotels, alongside theoretical education. Within this framework, and funded by GIZ, the Federation launched a tender to establish a learning management system to support these efforts and enable students to access training programs remotely in addition to attending onsite hotel-based training.
doubleLearning.goal1: Provide advanced, multimedia training content accessible online.
doubleLearning.goal2: Support and enhance the vocational education system in the tourism sector.
doubleLearning.goal3: Manage courses and training programs via a user-friendly interface.
doubleLearning.goal4: Accurately monitor and evaluate trainees' performance.

transitionTpl.title: Support Transition to the Labor Market Project
transitionTpl.description: The 'Support Transition to the Labor Market' project, funded by the European Union and the Egyptian government, is one of the training initiatives implemented by the Federation in cooperation with the Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities and the TVET Egypt program.
transitionTpl.point1: Project training activities started in March 2019.
transitionTpl.point2: A total of 13,157 trainees from the existing workforce received practical and theoretical training in the following tourism governorates: Cairo, Giza, Alexandria, South Sinai, Red Sea, Luxor, and Aswan.
transitionTpl.point3: Additionally, 8,613 workers received awareness training on environmental topics and COVID-19 preventive measures, bringing the total number of trainees to 21,770.
transitionTpl.point4: The project was completed on April 30, 2021.

cooking.title: Culinary Arts Training Centers
cooking.description1: The Egyptian Tourism Federation has established specialized training centers for culinary arts to prepare qualified professional chefs through practical programs designed according to international standards in collaboration with the British City & Guilds Foundation.
cooking.description2: Currently, a study is underway to restart the centers in one of the leading tourism governorates to meet the needs of the tourism labor market.
